# Bee Pollen

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="bee-pollen-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="bee-pollen-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="bee-pollen-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Bee Pollen in the HMI library has 394 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic, nickel, chromium, aluminium, antimony, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, Ag, Ba, Be, Bi, Ca, Ga, Ge, K, Li, Mg, Mo, <a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as bee Pollen

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers bee Pollen in 2 forms kept separate in every comparison: bee Pollen, as sold (328 results) and bee Pollen, dried (66 results).<sup <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-bee-pollen" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-bee-pollen-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of bee pollen, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach bee Pollen

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>

No study in the library compared bee Pollen from contaminated and ordinary settings, so the routes by which metals reach it are not measured here.



<a id="ranges-by-source-region-and-variety"></a>
## Which forms and regions measured lower

<a id="hmi-ing-013"></a>
<a id="how-do-concentrations-vary-by-origin-growing-conditions-variety-and-harvest-period"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-014"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-distinguishes-within-lot-between-lot-supplier-and-production-system-variation"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-015"></a>
<a id="which-comparisons-support-a-sourcing-decision-and-where-would-geographic-or-supplier-generalization-be-unjustified"></a>

In one study, lead across 8 groups of bee Pollen ranged from 59 µg/kg (L8: rural, no highway or industry nearby, Konya) to 180 µg/kg (L4: urban fringe, south of city, Konya); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/bayir2022-konya-honey-pollen-heavy-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bayir H, Aygun A · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bayir2022-konya-honey-pollen-heavy-metals">Heavy metal in honey bees, honey and pollen produced in different locations of Konya province in Turkey</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Research Square preprint, posted 1 March 2022 (version 1)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bayir2022-konya-honey-pollen-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, lead across 6 groups of bee Pollen ranged from 90 µg/kg (sample 5, collected 2 June 2019, Gory Zlotnickie apiary) to 220 µg/kg (sample 6, collected 20 July 2019, Gory Zlotnickie apiary); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/matuszewska2021-poland-bee-pollen-propolis-royal-jelly|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Matuszewska E, Klupczynska A, Maciołek K, Kokot ZJ, Matysiak J · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/matuszewska2021-poland-bee-pollen-propolis-royal-jelly">Multielemental Analysis of Bee Pollen, Propolis, and Royal Jelly Collected in West-Central Poland</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 26(9):2415</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/matuszewska2021-poland-bee-pollen-propolis-royal-jelly">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<a id="trade-offs-and-failure-modes"></a>
## Trade-offs and limits of controls

<a id="hmi-ing-022"></a>
<a id="can-an-intervention-increase-another-contaminant-or-redistribute-contamination-to-a-by-product"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-023"></a>
<a id="what-effects-on-nutrition-yield-sensory-quality-stability-and-waste-streams-were-measured"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-024"></a>
<a id="what-costs-constraints-adverse-effects-or-failure-modes-are-documented-and-which-are-unknown"></a>

Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.



<a id="sampling-and-testing"></a>
## Testing bee Pollen for metals

<a id="hmi-ing-025"></a>
<a id="what-sampling-design-is-appropriate-for-the-ingredient-heterogeneity-lot-and-decision"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-026"></a>
<a id="which-methods-species-measurements-validation-evidence-and-reporting-limits-are-needed"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-027"></a>
<a id="what-can-a-certificate-of-analysis-or-non-detect-establish-and-what-remains-untested"></a>

Results depend on the method and its reporting limit. Reporting limits for lead ranged from 90 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food) to 100 µg/kg (Grembecka et al. 2013), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/grembecka2013-poland-honeys-bee-products-minerals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Grembecka M, Szefer P · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/grembecka2013-poland-honeys-bee-products-minerals">Evaluation of honeys and bee products quality based on their mineral composition using multivariate techniques</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Monitoring and Assessment 185:4033-4047</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/grembecka2013-poland-honeys-bee-products-minerals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

A useful lot result names the form, the basis and a quantification limit well below the limit that applies.
